items.prompt:
A student sees the word 'helpless'. What is the root word, and what does the suffix '-less' tell you about the meaning?
A) Root: help; '-less' means 'without', so 'helpless' means 'without help'
B) Root: less; '-help' means 'needing', so 'helpless' means 'needing help'
C) Root: helpless; there is no suffix
items.answer: A) Root: help; '-less' means 'without', so 'helpless' means 'without help'

steps: Identify the suffix: '-less' is added to the END of the root word.
Remove '-less' from 'helpless': the root word is 'help'.
The suffix '-less' means 'without', so 'helpless' = without help.

items.prompt:
Which two-syllable word has a long vowel in the first syllable?
A) rabbit
B) frozen
C) mitten

steps: Break each word into syllables: rab-bit, fro-zen, mit-ten.
'rab-bit': first syllable 'rab' has a short /a/ sound.
'fro-zen': first syllable 'fro' has a long /oh/ sound (the vowel says its name).
'mit-ten': first syllable 'mit' has a short /i/ sound.

items.prompt:
The word 'unbelievable' contains two prefixes. Which two prefixes do you see?
A) un- and be-
B) un- and -able
C) be- and -able

steps: A prefix comes before the root word.
'un-' is the first prefix (means 'not').
'be-' is added before the root 'lieve' (believe).
'-able' is a suffix (comes at the end), not a prefix.

items.prompt:
A student reads the word 'coat'. Which vowel team is used, and what sound does it make?
A) 'oa' — makes the long /oh/ sound
B) 'oa' — makes the short /o/ sound
C) 'ot' — makes the long /oh/ sound

steps: The word 'coat' contains the vowel team 'oa'.
The vowel team 'oa' makes the long /oh/ sound.
Say it aloud: /koht/ — the 'o' says its name.

items.prompt:
Which word correctly uses the suffix '-ment' to mean 'the result of' an action?
A) movement
B) moveless
C) remover

steps: The suffix '-ment' means 'the result of' or 'the act of'.
'movement' = move + -ment: the result of moving.
'moveless' uses '-less', not '-ment'.
'remover' uses 're-' and '-er', not '-ment'.

items.prompt:
A student must decode 'trumpet'. She splits it as 'trum-pet'. Is that correct?
A) Yes — 'trum-pet' is the correct split
B) No — it should be 'tr-umpet'
C) No — it should be 'trump-et'
items.answer: A) Yes — 'trum-pet' is the correct split

steps: Say 'trumpet' aloud and clap: trum-pet.
The word splits between the two consonants 'm' and 'p': trum | pet.
Both syllables — 'trum' and 'pet' — have one vowel each, which is the pattern for two-syllable words.

items.prompt:
Which word has the r-controlled vowel 'ur'?
A) purse
B) pure
C) pole

steps: R-controlled vowels are vowels followed by 'r' that change the vowel sound.
'purse' — the vowel 'u' is followed by 'r': /pur/, making the /er/ sound.
'pure' — the 'e' after the 'r' is silent; the main vowel is 'u' making a long /yoo/ sound.
'pole' — no r-controlled vowel.

items.prompt:
A student reads the word 'payment'. What prefix and suffix are attached to the root 'pay'?
A) prefix: none; suffix: -ment
B) prefix: pay-; suffix: -ment
C) prefix: -ment; suffix: none

steps: Look at the beginning: there is no added prefix before 'pay'.
Look at the end: '-ment' is added after 'pay' (the root word).
So 'payment' = root 'pay' + suffix '-ment' (meaning the act of paying).

items.prompt:
Which word is irregularly spelled — it does NOT sound the way it is spelled?
A) wish
B) said
C) jump

steps: Try sounding each word out using phonics.
'wish': /w/ /i/ /sh/ — sounds exactly as spelled. Regular.
'said': if you sound it out, you might say /sayd/, but the real pronunciation is /sed/. Irregular!
'jump': /j/ /u/ /m/ /p/ — sounds exactly as spelled. Regular.

items.prompt:
A student sees the suffix '-ness' in 'darkness'. What does '-ness' mean?
A) without dark
B) the state of being dark
C) to make dark again
items.answer: B) the state of being dark

steps: The suffix '-ness' means 'the state or quality of being'.
'darkness' = dark + -ness = the state of being dark.
'-less' would mean 'without'. '-re' would mean 'again'. '-ness' means 'the state of being'.

items.prompt:
Which word has the vowel team 'ee' making the long /ee/ sound?
A) seed
B) send
C) shed

steps: 'seed' has the vowel team 'ee', which makes the long /ee/ sound: /seed/.
'send' has only the short vowel 'e': /send/.
'shed' has only the short vowel 'e': /shed/.

items.prompt:
How many syllables does 'together' have?
A) 2
B) 3
C) 4

steps: Clap as you say the word: to-geth-er.
Three claps = three syllables.
Each syllable has a vowel sound: /tuh/ /geth/ /er/.

items.prompt:
A student reads 'the bird sat on a perch'. Both 'bird' and 'perch' contain r-controlled vowels. What sounds do 'ir' and 'er' make?
A) Both make the /er/ sound
B) 'ir' makes /eye/ and 'er' makes /ee/
C) Both make the /ar/ sound

steps: R-controlled vowels 'ir', 'er', and 'ur' all make the same /er/ sound.
'bird' — the 'ir' makes /er/: /berd/.
'perch' — the 'er' makes /er/: /perch/.
Both sound the same even though they use different vowel letters.

items.prompt:
What does the prefix 're-' mean in 'reread'?
A) not reading
B) reading again
C) reading fast

steps: The prefix 're-' means 'again'.
'reread' = re- + read = to read again.
If you did not understand a sentence, you reread it — you read it again.

items.prompt:
Which word has a long vowel sound AND a suffix?
A) coldness
B) stamp
C) brick

steps: 'coldness' = cold (long /oh/ sound in 'cold') + suffix '-ness'.
The vowel 'o' in 'cold' makes the long /oh/ sound.
The suffix '-ness' is added at the end, meaning 'the state of being cold'.
'stamp' and 'brick' have short vowels and no suffixes.
